title: Symmetry of the Ramsey numbers
statement: For natural numbers $k$ and $l$, let $r(k,l)$ denote the Ramsey number: the least $n$ such that every simple graph on $n$ vertices contains either a clique on $k$ vertices or an independent set on $l$ vertices. Then $r(k,l) = r(l,k)$.
hypotheses_covered: k and l range over the natural numbers
replaced:
\emph{For all \texttt{k} and \texttt{l}, \texttt{r(k, l) = r(l, k)}.}

7.2.1 Show that, for all $k$ and $l$, $r(k, l) = r(l, k)$.

Clearly, $S$ is a clique of $G$ if and only if $S$ is an independent set of
$G^c$, and so the two concepts are complementary.
